profiles.Summary: Final Fantasy XIV Online runs well on the Steam Deck under Proton, achieving stable 40–60 fps at medium settings thanks to its relatively modest GPU requirements that align closely with the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU. As an MMO, performance can dip in crowded areas like major cities, so frame caps and TDP limits are recommended to keep thermals and battery life manageable.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum requirements (GTX 970 target, which the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU approaches at low-medium settings) and general MMO performance patterns on the hardware. On first run, check frame rate in a major city hub — if it drops below your cap, lower Shadow Quality and NPC display count first.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling keeps the GPU load low for maximum battery longevity. The 8 W TDP limit is enough to sustain 30 fps in most open-world areas, though very crowded city hubs may still dip briefly.

KnownIssues: Crowded areas (e.g., Limsa Lominsa, Ul'dah) can cause significant frame drops due to many player characters being rendered simultaneously.
The game requires a Square Enix account and online login, which may occasionally cause authentication issues under Proton.
Some UI elements and text can appear very small at 1280x800 — use the in-game font/HUD size scaling options.
The launcher may require additional Proton tweaks or a first-run workaround to get past the login screen on some Proton versions.

MaxPerformance.Notes: At native 1280x800 with high settings, FFXIV looks its best on the Deck and holds 60 fps in most open-world and dungeon content; expect drops to 45–50 fps in major city hubs or during large-scale raids with many players on screen.

Optimal.Notes: A 40 Hz refresh rate with a matching frame cap gives perfectly smooth motion and is the sweet spot for FFXIV on Deck; FSR upscaling from 1024x640 keeps the image sharp while giving the GPU enough headroom to hold 40 fps even in moderately busy city areas.
